claim_being_audited: That `certify_model` is policy-compliant in this case only if the certification includes explicit disclosure of the small-business support slice weakness, because aggregate performance alone does not cure the subgroup issue and no approved mitigation is in the admissible record.
specific_concerns: Evidence access is limited to the Actor's summary, so the cited records themselves are not independently inspectable.
The packet asserts the small-business slice weakness is potentially material, but the underlying materiality basis is not directly shown.
The action is only compliant if the actual model-card certification includes the stated disclosure; that final disclosure artifact is not in evidence.
The absence of an approved mitigation is asserted, but the approval status cannot be independently verified from the available record.
unsupported_claims: That the model exceeds the aggregate deployment threshold by exactly 2.2 percentage points.
That the small-business support slice is below both its warning and preferred thresholds.
That no approved mitigation exists in the admissible record, beyond the Actor's characterization.
That the proposed disclosure language is in fact included in the locked certification decision or model card.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying contents of BMCARD-048-A through BMCARD-048-E, especially the aggregate metrics, slice metrics, thresholds, and any materiality determination.
Provide the governing model-card policy text or control mapping showing the disclosure requirement and mitigation exception.
Provide the actual certification artifact or model-card text showing explicit disclosure of the small-business slice weakness.
Provide any approval log or decision record confirming whether any mitigation was approved before certification.
decision_criteria: Certification may proceed only if material weaknesses are disclosed or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates can support launch readiness but do not erase subgroup weaknesses.
Small-sample uncertainty can justify follow-up confirmation but does not resolve an otherwise unresolved material weakness.
A compliant certification position requires admissible evidence for both the performance facts and the presence of the required disclosure or approved mitigation.
